messages:
alex.chen: hey all — onboarding hiccup. I'm migrating from my old MBP to a new company MacBook Air. Migration Assistant fails with: "Could not mount encrypted user volume (error -69545)". FileVault's on. I also need my SSH keys + Keychain items transferred. Do I need to disable FileVault first or can IT push something? Need temp admin to run a few commands if so. Screenshot: https://img.company/screencap-err.png

it_helpdesk: welcome @alex.chen :wave: we can help. quick Qs before we flip anything: what macOS version on old Mac and new Mac? also please paste outputs of `diskutil apfs list` and `fdesetup status` (just the lines, no secrets).

alex.chen: new MBP: macOS 13.5.1, old: macOS 12.6. diskutil output:
```
/dev/disk1 (synthesized):
   APFS Container Scheme - Physical Store disk0s2
   +-> Physical Store disk0s2

   APFS Volume disk1s1 - Container disk1 (Encrypted)
   APFS Volume disk1s2 - Data
```
and `fdesetup status` -> "FileVault is On."

mdm-bot: MDM notice — enrollment profile pushed to device at 2024-09-03T15:22:10Z. Status: profile installed; compliance: pending policies (device not yet marked compliant until migration completes).

it_helpdesk: ok. Plan A (non-invasive): create a temporary local admin account on the new Mac (not your personal account), run Migration Assistant from the old Mac to that admin user, then use `sudo` to chown files into your enterprise account. High level steps:
1) Create local admin: System Settings > Users & Groups > Add user (Admin).
2) On old Mac: Migration Assistant -> To another Mac. On new Mac: Migration Assistant -> From a Mac. Choose the new temp admin as destination.
3) After migration, log into your normal enterprise account, then run as temp admin: `sudo chown -R alex.chen /Users/alex.chen` and `chmod 700 ~/.ssh` plus `chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_rsa` to fix perms.
Notes: do NOT copy Keychain files manually if possible — use Keychain Access app (File > Import Items) to import exported keychain items.

jordan_devops: also for SSH keys: if you have the private key on the old mac, copy `~/.ssh` to an encrypted external drive or use `rsync -a --progress ~/.ssh /Volumes/Encrypted/` then on new mac `rsync -a --progress /Volumes/Encrypted/.ssh ~`. after copy run: `chmod 700 ~/.ssh && chmod 600 ~/.ssh/*` and `ssh-add -K ~/.ssh/id_rsa` to store passphrase in macOS keychain. If you're using passphrases, you'll be prompted once.

it_helpdesk: corporate policy reminder: do not export corporate secrets to personal cloud. Use company-approved encrypted USB (we can provide). If you prefer we can push a one-time admin profile for 2 hours instead of creating a local admin yourself. Want us to push that?

claire_w: welcome aboard @alex.chen — ping me if you need any repo or GitHub access after keys are back.

alex.chen: happy to have IT push the temp admin, yes please. thanks!

it_helpdesk: done — pushed `temp-admin-2h` profile at 15:27. You'll receive a secure message via Okta with the temporary admin username. When you log into that admin, you'll have elevated rights for 2 hours.

mdm-bot: MDM notice — device compliance updated at 2024-09-03T15:30:35Z. Status: compliant.

alex.chen: ran migration under temp admin; followed the rsync flow for `~/.ssh`, imported keychain items via Keychain Access, fixed perms, and re-added keys with `ssh-add -K`. FileVault stayed enabled and login works. All good :tada:

it_helpdesk: awesome — glad it worked. we'll revoke the temp-admin automatically at the 2-hour mark. If anything else pops up (VPN certs, SSO keychain), reopen this thread or ping IT.

alex.chen: thanks everyone, huge help! :heart:
